newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIANS DO NOT EXPECT NEW ELECTIONS - POLL.
newsitem.headline: BELGIANS DO NOT EXPECT NEW ELECTIONS - POLL.

text.p: Nearly half the Belgian citizens think that the PS francophone socialist party, the focus of a bribery scandal, should leave the government, but less than a quarter expects elections in the coming months, a poll showed.

A poll of 2,000 Belgians published by daily La Deniere Heure on Thursday showed 87.5 percent believes that former PS chairman Guy Spitaels was aware of kickbacks allegedly paid to the PS by French aviation firm Dassault in 1989.
Two former PS officials were arrested last week and charged with corruption in the Dassault case, sparking a leadership crisis in the PS and calls for elections from the opposition.
Asked whether the PS should leave the government -- as the opposition wants -- 49 percent said 'yes'. But only 23.5 percent of those polled expected elections in the coming months.
Louis Michel, chairman on the francophone liberal party PRL, on Thursday offered to replace the PS in Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene's centre-left coalition.
His proposal was shrugged off by the Dutch-speaking christian democratic party CVP, the largest party in the four-party coalition.
